---
title: "Pipeline"
---

Scripts are numbered in run order. Each reads what the previous step wrote and writes to
`<DATA_ROOT>/data/outputs/`:

```bash
uv run python scripts/20_subsets/21_prepare_input_data.py
```

Most steps take minutes. On a 24-thread machine with 208 sites,
`21_prepare_input_data.py` takes about 40 minutes, `31_shap.py` about 20,
`32_validate_shap_methods.py` about 85 and `41_binagg_per_site.py` about 13.

## Run variants

Every stage from 21 onward has a `VARIANT` constant, except script 51. Script 86 loops
over a list, `VARIANTS`. An empty string reads and writes the
baseline paths. Any other value adds a folder level on both sides, so a variant reads
`20_subsets/<VARIANT>/` and writes `30_shap/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/`. A stage fails on a
missing file if its predecessor has not run with the same variant.

| VARIANT | Change | Output through |
|---|---|---|
| empty | None, the published run | Every stage |
| `deep-sm` | Deepest usable soil water layer per site | Stage 49, plus the ALE stages 32 and 46 |
| `blocked-cv` | Leave-one-year-out instead of a shuffled split | Stage 49 |
| `no_ta` | Air temperature dropped from the predictors | Stage 41 |
| `no_vpd` | VPD dropped from the predictors | Stage 31 |
| `mirrored-stages` | Stage sequence in which VPD escalates and extreme soil dryness is added last | Stage 44 only |
| `factorial-cells` | Four soil water classes by four VPD classes, temperature left free | Stage 44 only |

Scripts from 41 onward also take `SITE_SUBSET`, either `""` for all sites or
`"deeper-only"` for the 128 sites with a soil water layer below layer 1. With the empty
variant and `deep-sm`, this subset gives a matched pair: the same 128 sites at their
shallowest and at their deepest layer. Scripts 45, 46, 51, 57, 61, 64, 66 to 68, 80,
85 to 87 and 89 take no subset.

`31_shap.py` and `32_validate_shap_methods.py` take `SITES` and `MAX_SITES` to limit a
run for timing.

| Script | Function | Writes |
|--------|----------|--------|
| `00_find_overlaps.py` | Finds sites in both AmeriFlux and FLUXNET-SHUTTLE and deletes their AmeriFlux folders. Already applied, do not rerun | `10_datasets/` |

| `12_create_parquet.py` | Merges the datasets of each site by source priority | `12_parquet_merged/`, `12_datasets_info_parquet.csv` |
| `13_check_available_vars.py` | Records which of NEE, LE, GPP, RECO, TA, VPD, SWIN and SWC exist per site, and under which name | `13_datasets_info_parquet_vars.csv` |
| `13b_check_available_vars_SWC.py` | Reports the coverage of every soil water layer per site, within the peak months and against layer 1 | `13b_variables_coverage_summary.csv`, `13b_variables_per_site.csv` |
| `14_collect_basic_stats.py` | Collects record counts, date ranges and basic statistics per variable | `14_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats.csv` |
| `15_remove_sites.py` | Applies the inclusion criteria | `15_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites.csv` |
| `16a` to `16d`, `16_download_era5_mat_map.py` | Download ERA5 1991 to 2020 normals from Google Earth Engine and the Copernicus CDS | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020*/` |
| `17_add_era5_info.py` | Adds MAT and MAP per site from the flux product's ERA5 file or ERA5-Land, with source and reason | `17_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites_era5.csv` |

## 20_subsets: model input

`21_prepare_input_data.py` builds the subset the models see, per site:

1. keep the four months with the highest mean GPP
2. keep measured NEE only (quality flag 0)
3. keep daytime records, `SW_IN_POT > 20`
4. balance the record so every month contributes the same number of years
5. drop records with any missing predictor
6. derive ET from LE and TA, and NEP as `-NEE`
7. z-score every variable within the site

`SWC_LAYER = "shallow"` uses `SWC_F_MDS_1`, and `"deepest"` uses the deepest usable layer
per site (see [Methods](methods.qmd#soil-water-layer)). CD-Ygb stores VPD in Pa, and this
script keeps it. The z-scores are unaffected. Scripts 47, 48, 54, 58, 68 and 81, which
convert VPD to kPa, divide the CD-Ygb values by 100. Script 45 does not, so its per-site
medians for CD-Ygb are in Pa. The cross-site medians and quartiles of Supplementary
Table 4 are the same at two decimals with and without the conversion. It writes one
parquet per site to `21_subsets_parquet/` and
the summary `21_SUBSETS_parquet_vars_stats_subsets.csv`, which records the soil water
layer used per site. `N_WORKERS = 3` by default, and the largest sites need about 3 GB
per worker.

`22_data_flow.py` counts the records each filter removes per site and checks its final
count against script 21. Of the delivered half-hourly records, 7.1 percent reach the
models. The quality filter removes the most.

## 30_shap: models and attribution

`31_shap.py` fits one XGBoost regressor per site and computes SHAP values. Switches at
the top of the file:

| Switch | Values |
|---|---|
| `FLUX` | `NEP_ZSCORE` (published), `GPP_ZSCORE`, `RECO_ZSCORE` or `ET_ZSCORE`, each with its own output folder |
| `CV_STRATEGY` | `random` (published, shuffled 5-fold) or `blocked` (leave one year out) |
| `FEATURE_SET` | `full`, `no_vpd` or `no_ta` |
| `TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS` | `False` for the analysis, `True` for the hyperparameter search |

Within each fold, 80 percent of the records are split into 68 percent for fitting and
12 percent for early stopping. The model explains the held-out 20 percent, so every SHAP
value comes from a model that never saw the record. The script writes per-site parquet
and csv files with predictors, SHAP values and predictions, plus one csv of fold metrics.
Unchanged sites give bit-identical output between runs.

`32_validate_shap_methods.py` fits one model per site on an 85/15 split, computes ALE
curves on 100 grid points per predictor and writes `{SITE}_ale_curves_{TARGET}.csv`.

## 40_aggregation: results across sites

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `41_binagg_per_site.py` | Bins each site's SHAP values on a two-variable grid with shared edges, for five variable pairs (TA-VPD, SWC-VPD, TA-SWC, ET-VPD, ET-SWC) |
| `42_binagg_across_sites.py` | Averages the site grids, one vote per site |
| `43_binagg_across_igbp.py` | Averages the site grids per forest type |
| `44_agg_per_scenario.py` | Computes SHAP means within the stress stages, per site and across sites. `STAGE_SEQUENCE` is `"published"`, `"mirrored"` or `"factorial"` |
| `45_stage_distributions.py` | Computes driver medians and quartiles within each stage, in standardized and measured units |
| `46_ale_thresholds.py` | Puts the per-site ALE curves on one grid, takes the highest crossing from positive to negative of each and averages them, overall and per forest type |
| `47_threshold_robustness.py` | Re-estimates the VPD threshold eighteen ways, with a bootstrap over sites, the 23-setting estimator sweep and leave-one-site-out. Feeds Table 1 |
| `48_threshold_exceedance.py` | Computes the share of peak-season daytime half-hours above the threshold, per site and forest type |
| `49_biome_thresholds.py` | Estimates one threshold per site (highest crossing from positive to negative) and compares forest types with Kruskal-Wallis and Holm-corrected pairwise tests |

Run 41 first, then 42 and 43. Run 44 any time after 31, 46 after 32 and 49 after 41. Run
47 after 46 and after the `deep-sm`, `deeper-only`, `blocked-cv` and `no_ta` runs have
reached stage 41. Run 48 after 47 and 49. Bins covered by fewer than half the sites are
dropped.

## 50_figures

Figure scripts write to `50_plots/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/<SITE_SUBSET>/`, so a variant
never overwrites a published figure. Script 53 writes Supplementary Fig. 3 to the folder
without the variant level, under its own name. Scripts 55, 57, 59, 60 and 65 read the
stage 40 files of 47, 46, 45, 48 and 49, in that order. Script 68 reads those of 41, 47
and 49. Scripts 59, 61, 62, 63 and 64 read the stage 80 files of 89, 87, 81, 82 and 86,
in that order. See [Figures](figures.qmd).

## 80_info: sensitivity checks

These scripts compute numbers quoted in the paper and write to
`80_info/<FLUX>/conditional/<VARIANT>/<SITE_SUBSET>/`. Scripts 80 and 85 to 87 write to
`80_info/<FLUX>/`. Where a supplementary table shows
the same numbers, a script of the 50s lays out the INFO file.

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `80_time_scale_coverage.py` | Measured share of a peak-season day, and the records and Stage 8 records left at daily, monthly and yearly resolution |
| `81_threshold_definitions.py` | Peak, steepest decline, crossing from positive to negative and minimum of the fitted VPD response, with range-edge flags |
| `82_threshold_vs_site_vpd_range.py` | Per-site thresholds by quartile of the site's maximum VPD, with all 208 sites in the quartiles. The direction of each driver's effect at every site goes to `82_INFO_DriverEffectDirection.csv` |
| `83_leave_region_out.py` | Threshold and Stage 8 attribution with Europe, North America or both removed |
| `84_short_record_sensitivity.py` | Threshold and Stage 8 attribution under minimum record lengths |
| `85_wue_vs_vpd.py` | Water use efficiency against VPD per site |
| `86_site_skill.py` | Site-level R^2^, RMSE, MAE and bias under both cross-validation splits, overall, in Stage 8 and in the high-VPD tail |
| `87_stage_cutoff_percentiles.py` | Empirical share of records below each stage cut-off, against the Gaussian share |
| `88_stage_order_test.py` | Net effect along the published and the mirrored stage order |
| `89_stage_matching.py` | Stage 7 against Stage 8 on matched records |

Scripts 83 and 84 use the median of the per-site thresholds, which sits about 0.07 kPa
below the crossing of the aggregated curve. Table 1 reports the crossing.

## 90_deposit: data deposit

These scripts write the files for the ETH Research Collection to
`<DATA_ROOT>/deposit_eth_research_collection/`. Script 91 also writes the Source Data for
the journal to `<DATA_ROOT>/submission_nature_communications/`. Script 93 lists every zip
archive already in the deposit folder in `MANIFEST.csv` and `ARCHIVES.csv`. Run 91 and 92
before 93, and put the code and documentation snapshots there first as well: the code with
`git archive --format=zip --prefix=ms-forests-vpd/` from the tagged commit as
`ms-forests-vpd_code.zip`, and `docs/_site/` rendered from the same commit as
`ms-forests-vpd_docs.zip`. Script 95 writes the
figures for this site and script 96 the Output columns page. Scripts 91 to 93 and 95 do a
dry run by default and write only with `--build`. Script 96 always writes the page and
writes `COLUMNS.csv` only with `--build`.

| Script | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `91_build_source_data.py` | The Source Data: the data file of every figure, table and Supplementary Data file of the main analysis, copied under a plain name (`Fig4_all_sites.csv`, `SupplementaryTable6.xlsx`), with a README |
| `92_build_demo_data.py` | `ms-forests-vpd_demo.zip`, the model input of one site (CH-Dav) with its published output, so script 31 can be tried without the full deposit (see Demo in the README) |
| `93_build_deposit_archives.py` | One uncompressed zip per output stage, with `MANIFEST.csv` and `ARCHIVES.csv` |
| `94_build_data_flow_chart.py` | `DATA_FLOW.html`, a zoomable chart of every script with the files it reads and writes, from `94_data_flow_graph.json` |
| `95_copy_figures_to_docs.py` | The 14 figures of the paper, scaled to 1600 px and 256 colors, in `docs/figures/` for the [Figures](figures.qmd) page |
| `96_build_column_reference.py` | The [Output columns](columns.qmd) page and `COLUMNS.csv`, from the descriptions in `96_column_dictionary.yaml`, checked against the header of every output file |

The reads and writes in `94_data_flow_graph.json` were taken from the code by hand. When
a script changes the files it reads or writes, update its entry there and rerun
script 94. It also writes a copy of the chart to `docs/data_flow.html` for this site.
